text:
alex: Heads-up — running long-context runs with paged KV cache on H100 and seeing steady GPU memory growth. Page table entry count keeps climbing even after 'evict' logs. Anyone seen this?

sam: I've seen something similar on A100 but only when batch-size >= 8 and continuous batching enabled. Might be a reclaim race.

maria: Can you paste a minimal repro and the exact flags? Also which model / tokenizer?

alex: repro steps below, small log snippet after ~50k tokens: 
```
# repro (toy)
./run_inference --model gpt-j-6b --context 120000 --batch-size 8 --kv-mode paged --kv-page-size 64k
# after ~50k tokens
[perf] page_table.size=131072 pages_allocated=124320 pages_free=2752
[perf] evict_pages called count=312 but freed=0
```

jin: fwiw profiler shows many host->device enqueue stalls and a flurry of page-table updates on stream0. H100 seems to keep page descriptors alive longer — TLB/ptl differences. On L4 the pattern is different (less growth).

priya: My suspicion: PageTable::evict_pages isn't doing an atomic exchange when clearing entries; a concurrent kernel can rebind the page and we lose the free list update. Could explain freed=0 even after evict calls.

kevin: Also worth noting batching heuristic: continuous-batching interleaves requests across streams which increases temporal locality churn in the allocator. Try `--disable-continuous-batching` or force single-stream for the KV allocator to see if it changes.

alex: Disabling continuous batching reduced growth rate but we still see fragmentation: free pages exist but allocator doesn't reuse same page index, keeps allocating new indices. Log snippet: 
``
pages_allocated=129840 pages_free=3120 reused_pages=48
```

maria: Can someone run a microbenchmark that toggles: (1) single vs multi-stream, (2) batching on/off, (3) kv-page-size 32k/64k/128k — and collect nvprof/cupti counters for memory reads/writes and inter-stream synchronization. Also add per-stream page alloc counters.

sam: I'll run A100/H100 comparison and upload traces to the perf bucket. Expect to have them by EOD.

priya: Quick patch idea: switch to atomic compare_exchange when nulling page_table entries and append freed page ids via lock-free free-list (use atomic head exchange). Add a short qdisc GC that coalesces fragmented free segments every N tokens. I have a local branch that reduces growth in my smoke tests. Opening PR #4382 for discussion. :thumbsup:

alex: Thanks — please add the microbench script to the PR. I'll attach the nvprof traces I have. For now we can land the GC workaround to mitigate customer impact.

ops-bot: test-cluster updated: perf/kv-paged-test nodes now have new cuda 12.2 driver, H100 and A100 sets available.

kevin: one more note — check cuda stream memory fences around page binding kernels. On H100 the scheduler interleaves kernels differently which can expose missing cudaStreamSynchronize or record/release ordering.

priya: agreed. I'll add extra stream fences in the dev branch and see if that makes the eviction durable.

alex: 👍 opening an issue with traces + commands now. tagging @maria @sam @priya for follow-ups.
